correctness.rationale: Write q=max_j(-Q_jj), so ||Q||_1=2q. Normalize q=1, exits (1,b,c), t=b+c. The nonzero eigenvalues of -Q have sum 1+t and product at most t+bc<=t+t²/4. If t>=1/2, their maximum real part is at least (1+t)/2>=3/4. Otherwise their discriminant is at least 1-2t and the larger real root is >=(1+t+sqrt(1-2t))/2>=3/4. Spectral radius of e^{-Q} then implies the bound. In the irreducible Q0 directed cycle with rates (1,1/4,1/4), the exact projective/Jordan decomposition P+exp(3h/4)(I-P+hN) with N²=0 and ||N||_1=4/3 gives ratio tending to 8/3. All identities verified symbolically and with a reproducible checker; the proof, not finite experiments, handles universal statements.
